texts: At the bier all faces turn to one Lord who has no face, and gold on the body cannot shape what has no shape.
bier, gold, formless Lord
doha with bier and gold about God having no form or name
Watching my uncle carried on a bier with his gold ring still on, I wondered who or what the God he talked about really was, since he never described a face or a shape for Him.
Write a doha at a bier where gold ornaments lie useless, saying that the God beyond all form and name cannot be dressed in jewels or carved in a likeness, for He has no body to adorn.
I would like a doha about a beggar asking the faceless, nameless God for alms, who gives without any form or body, and whom no one can describe in words or capture in any picture.
beggar, God without form
The beggar stretches his palms to the nameless, shapeless One, who gives in silence from beyond all names.
A beggar outside our colony told me, when I asked what god he prays to, that his God has no picture, no name and no shape, and yet gives him enough every day.
doha about the formless God and a beggar please
chakor bird, touchstone, formless One
Compose a doha comparing the chakor bird gazing at an unseen sky with the seeker who loves a God without form, and the touchstone that cannot weigh what has no shape, attribute or measure.
I tried to describe God to my little niece the way the chakor bird in her book stares at the sky, and found no touchstone of words could test what has no form, shape or name.
The chakor gazes at what no eye can hold; the touchstone cannot test the One beyond all name.
chakor bird and touchstone doha about the God who has no shape
After I was pricked by a thorn on a hike, I sat down and thought of a sword-edge of truth: the God I pray to has no face or shape, yet feels as real as that sharp pain.
No thorn can wound Him, no sword can cut Him: the formless One has neither body nor name to harm.
Write a doha about a thorn and a sword that can pierce any body but cannot touch the Lord who has no form, no name and no attributes, because He is beyond everything that can be described.
thorn, sword, formless God
doha with a thorn and a sword about the God with no shape or name
arrow doha about the God who has no form
arrow, nameless God
Please write a doha about an arrow that flies toward a target it cannot see, as the mind flies toward a God without form, name or attributes, who cannot be aimed at, imagined or described.
The arrow flies and finds no target, for the Lord has no outline for the mind to strike.
My archery coach says you must aim at nothing in particular and let the arrow go, which reminded me of how my teacher described God: without form or name, impossible to aim at.
doha with a physician; God has no form, no one can describe Him
physician, God without attributes
The physician told my mother, who is gravely ill, that no medicine can reach what the soul believes in, and my mother smiled and said her God has no name or face at all.
The physician reads the pulse and the veins, but cannot find the One who has no shape or name.
Compose a doha about a physician who can describe every part of the body but can never describe the formless Lord, who has no limbs, no face, no colour, and no name, yet fills everything.
My little son asked me today what God looks like, and I could not say what colour, what face or what name, because the God I know is beyond all of that.
doha about God having no form, shape or name at all
Please write a doha that says the divine cannot be given a face, a colour or a name by human imagination, for the Lord is beyond all forms and attributes and can only be known by being.
Beyond the reach of word and picture, beyond the shape that thought can draw, the One abides unnamed.
formless, nameless God
I want a doha for those who argue over what God looks like, saying that the Lord is without form, colour or name, beyond what any painter, sculptor or poet can show, and so the argument is pointless.
short doha, God is beyond name and form, no description fits
God beyond names
He has no face for the painter, no name for the singer: the Unnamed is nearer than the thought that seeks Him.
At a family dinner everyone argued over which form of God is the real one, and my grandfather just said quietly that the real one has no form at all.
When my daughter asked why we don't have a picture of God in our room, I found myself saying that He is too vast and too close to be put into any picture.
Please write a doha explaining that the Lord has no body, no colour and no shape, and is therefore not found in any image or description, but in the silent knowing beyond all words.
God without attributes
doha about the unnameable, formless supreme being plz
Shapeless as the wind, nameless as silence, the Lord is present where no description reaches.
swan, dew, formless Lord
swan and dew doha about the God who has no form
Watching a swan skim a pond at dawn with dew still on the grass, I realised I had no word at all for the thing I felt, nor a picture of the God behind it.

Write a doha about a swan drifting through morning dew, which cannot be held or described, and let it say that the Lord is like that: without form or name, felt only as presence beyond all attributes.
The swan leaves no mark on the water; the dew leaves no trace at noon; so too the Formless passes without footprint.
doha with an inn - god has no shape or name
Staying at an inn on a pilgrimage, I met an old man who told me, with total calm, that God has no form and no home to be visited, no matter how far I traveled.
inn, nameless God
Please write a doha about a night at an inn where many guests argue about what their God looks like, until one says gently that the Lord is without form or name and cannot be shown or drawn.
The inn hosts a hundred sects and a hundred pictures, but the One who has no picture is host to all.

Compose a doha about a heron that stands still as if it knows something, and say that the God who has no form or name is not found by pretending or posing, but by dropping all descriptions of the divine.
The heron stands in still water like an idea of stillness, while the Lord, who has no form, is stillness itself.
A heron stood motionless by the pond at dusk and I tried to pray to the unseen God, but all my images of Him dissolved, and I realised He has no image.
heron, God without form
doha with heron: God is formless, nameless, you can't picture Him
yogi and pearl doha about the God who has no name or form
yogi, pearl, formless
A yogi I met at the pearl dealers' lane told me his meditation is not on any figure, because God has no figure, only awareness beyond every image he could invent.
The yogi dives into silence and finds the pearl without a surface, the Lord with no form to hold.
Write a doha where a yogi sits and looks for God as a pearl in the deep, but discovers the pearl has no shape at all, since the Lord is formless and beyond all names and attributes.
doha: God has no form, no name, nothing you can say about Him
formless God, beyond words
I used to picture God as an old man in the sky, but now I think that was a child's idea and the truth has no figure, no name, nothing to picture.

Write a doha for a person who keeps trying to picture God and fails, assuring him that the divine is without form, shape, colour or name, and the failure of imagination is itself the beginning of knowing.
When thought lays down its brushes and speech lays down its names, the Formless stands revealed.

I need a doha explaining that the Lord has no name, no form, no attribute, and that everything we say about Him is only a finger pointing toward what cannot be said, which is greater than all description.
When I tried to write a prayer for my wedding I found that everything I wrote about God felt too small, since no word or picture ever fits the One who has no shape.
Words are small birds that fall before the nameless; the Formless is not caught in any syllable.
nameless, formless, beyond speech
plz doha on the attribute-less God no one can describe
Fire has a shape, the flame has a colour, but the Lord has neither; He is the One beyond all burning forms.
Please write a doha about fire that takes any shape it touches but cannot be held, saying God is like that: without any shape of His own, without name or attributes, though present in everything.
fire, formless God
doha with fire and the God who has no shape
Sitting around a bonfire with my friends, someone asked what God looks like and everyone fell silent, because no one could name a shape for something so much larger than the fire.
When the fire spread through our neighbour's shop, everyone said it was God's will, but I kept thinking: whose God, with what face, since mine has none.
The fire dances in a hundred forms yet has no shape of its own; the Formless takes no form but fills them all.
doha with fire - God has no form, no name, no attributes
fire, nameless Lord
Write a doha about a fire that consumes all forms and leaves nothing behind, and say that the Lord who has no form, no face and no name is what remains when every image is burnt away.
Compose a doha about milk poured into water, merging until no one can separate them, and say that the Lord has no form of His own, no name, no boundary, and so cannot be marked off from the world.
Milk poured into water leaves no line between; so the Formless blends with all, with nothing to mark Him apart.
milk, formless Lord
When I mixed milk into my tea this morning, I thought about how the divine, as my teacher taught, has no outline you can point to, since it is blended into everything.
doha with milk, about God having no shape or name
My mother lets me taste only plain food when I'm sick, and bitter gourd with salt is a childhood medicine; it makes me think the God I pray to has no flavour or shape, yet heals everything.
doha with bitter gourd and salt about the formless, nameless God
bitter gourd, salt, formless
Bitter gourd and salt, both ordinary; the Lord, without taste or shape, is the secret in all.
Please write a doha about salt dissolving unseen in a dish of bitter gourd, so that its presence is felt but never seen; the Lord is like that, without form, name or attributes, yet present in all.
At the closed door of my old school I tried to remember what I'd been taught about God, and realised no picture was ever given, only a feeling that He is formless and everywhere.
Knock on the door of the visible and find it opens onto the Unformed, who has no door and no wall.
door, formless Lord
Write a doha about a door that cannot open to God because He has no shape to walk through it, no name to be called by it, no body to enter; He is already in the room and outside it.
doha with a door about the God with no form or name
At the grand palace tour, the guide described each golden statue and painting of the gods, and I whispered to my wife that the God I pray to has no form and cannot be painted.
Write a doha about a palace filled with portraits and carved figures of divinity, saying that the true Lord is beyond them all, without form, name or attribute, and no palace can hold Him.
palace doha, god has no shape or name, can't be depicted
palace, nameless Lord
The palace walls are hung with a thousand faces of God, yet the One has no face and dwells in none of them.
I want a doha with a skeleton and a leaf: the body falls away to bones, the leaf turns to dust, but the Lord who has no body, colour or name remains beyond all forms that rise and fall.
skeleton, leaf, formless Lord
Skeleton and leaf, both shed their forms; the Formless stays, untouched by what falls.
Walking through the autumn lane after visiting the skeleton exhibit at the museum, I picked up a leaf and wondered what part of all this is God, if God has no body or face.
doha: skeleton, leaf, and the God who has no body or name
lock, mountain, formless Lord
The mountain keeps its secrets under heavy lock, but the Formless needs no lock, for He has no shape to hide.
Write a doha where a mountain stands vast and a lock guards a treasure, yet the God who has no form, no name and no attributes cannot be locked away, climbed to, or reached by any path.
doha with a lock and mountain, god has no shape or name
We climbed the mountain to reach a locked chamber and found it sealed, and my father said it did not matter because the God he prays to has no shape to be put behind a lock.
skeleton, needle, formless God
My grandmother, threading a needle by the window, told me that she once asked a wise man what God looks like and he said a skeleton has more form than the God of her prayers.
Needle and skeleton, small and sharp, can never pierce or measure the One without form.
doha with skeleton and needle: God has no shape, no name
Please write a doha in which a needle can stitch the cloth and a skeleton holds the body, but neither can describe or hold the Lord, who is without any form, name or attributes whatsoever.
Let the temple fall silent, for the One who has no face is not summoned by any sound.
After years of visiting the same temple, I started to feel that the God I really meet has no face, no name, and cannot be seen in any carved corner of it.
doha about a temple and the faceless God beyond all forms

Write a doha about a temple full of carved figures where the visitors seek the shape of God, and say that the Lord is without form, beyond every figure and name, and cannot be confined by any building.
temple, formless Lord
The spinning wheel turns, the tree gives shade, but nothing spun can shape the Formless nor shade hold Him.
spinning wheel and tree doha - God has no form or name
Compose a doha about a spinning wheel turning beneath a great tree, where the weaver thinks of God and cannot give Him any shape, because the Lord has no form, no name and no attribute.
spinning wheel, tree, formless
My grandmother spins at her spinning wheel beneath the neem tree, and when I asked what God looked like she just smiled and said He had no face, only presence.
Please write a doha with a bee and a river: the bee can be seen, the river can be heard, but the Lord has no form to see and no sound to hear, being beyond all names and attributes.
bee, river, formless God
Beside the river, a bee circled my head while I was thinking about how impossible it is to picture God, who has no body, no colour, no name.
Bee and river, both can be named; the Lord cannot, for He is the silence in which names arise.
doha with a bee and a river about the God who has no shape
tortoise and grindstone doha about the God with no form, no name
Slow tortoise, grindstone worn thin, both are shaped by time; the Formless has no shape for time to wear.
Write a doha with a tortoise and a grindstone, saying that things that can be seen and touched grow old and wear away, but the Lord, who has no form, no name and no attributes, never changes.
My tortoise is older than me, and the grindstone in my grandmother's courtyard is older still, but my teacher says the God behind everything has no shape to grow old.
tortoise, grindstone, nameless Lord
rainbird, formless God
I heard a rainbird calling for the rain all week, and thought of how I call out to a God I cannot see or name or draw, who has no shape at all.
The rainbird cries for a rain it has never touched; so I cry for a Lord who has no name.
doha with a rainbird about the God who has no form
Please write a doha about a rainbird calling to the sky for a drop, and say that the devotee calls just so to a God who has no face, no name and no attributes, beyond what any call can capture.

Compose a doha for someone who thinks God must have a definite face and name, telling him gently that the Lord is without form, attributes or limits, and that all human images are only small, kind lies.
beyond name and form
My cousin was upset that I do not keep a picture of God in my room; I tried to explain that the God I believe in has no face or name to frame.
doha on the God who cannot be pictured or named
Whatever you imagine, He is beyond; whatever you name, He is without name; whatever you paint, He has no colour.
Please write a doha that says the divine cannot be limited to any single name, shape or description, as it is beyond all attributes, quality and measure, yet closer than the breath.
short doha on the God with no attributes or form
When people ask me what religion I follow I struggle to answer, because my sense of the divine has no name or picture attached to it at all.
No name can hold Him, no shape can bind Him; He is the One beyond every word the heart can form.
attributeless, nameless, formless
The oil press squeezes the grain to find its essence; the Formless is the essence that no press can find, having no body.
Please write a doha about an oil press that extracts oil from the grain but cannot extract the Lord, who has no form, name or attribute to be pressed out, only a presence beyond all measure.
oil press, formless Lord
doha with an oil press about the God with no shape or name
My uncle runs an old oil press and says he has pressed every kind of grain but never found anything to hold up and call God, because the God he honours has no shape.
washerman, river, formless God

Compose a doha about a washerman at the river scrubbing cloth, who knows many things but cannot say what God looks like, for the Lord has no form, no colour and no name, and flows through all like the river.
The washerman by our river told me he prays every day, but when I asked to whom, he said to the One who has no face and no name, who is in the water and in the cloth.
washerman and river doha about God having no form or name
The washerman cleans the cloth in the river, but the river's source has no shape, and the Lord has no name.
Cuckoo, your song is sweet, but you cannot sing the Name of the One who has none, nor draw the face of the Faceless.
Write a doha about the cuckoo calling in the mango grove, whose sweet cry cannot describe the Lord, who is without form, name or attributes, and is only intuited in the silence between the notes.
doha with a cuckoo about the God who has no form
cuckoo, formless God
A cuckoo called from the garden all morning while I tried in vain to explain to my daughter what God is like, and the only answer I could give was that He has no form at all.
Standing at sunset watching my shadow stretch across the road, I realised I keep trying to give God a shape too, though He is beyond shape, name and every outline.
Write a doha about a shadow that follows every body and takes its shape, while the Lord who is without form, name or attributes casts no shadow, and cannot be traced or imagined in any outline.
shadow, formless Lord
doha with a shadow about God having no shape or name
The shadow takes the shape of what it follows; the Formless has no shape for any shadow to follow.
My friend who loves comparative religion kept asking me to sum up my idea of God, and I could only say He has no description, no shape, no name, no picture.
doha on how the true God has no name, no shape, no description

Please write a doha explaining that the Lord is above and beyond all forms and attributes, that nothing we say about Him is quite right, and that the highest knowing is the surrender of all descriptions.
Silence is the only name that does not lie about Him, whose form is no form and whose being is beyond being.
beyond description, nameless
moneylender, formless God
The moneylender weighs every coin, but who can weigh the Nameless, who has no form and no measure?
The moneylender in our lane insists that his god is a shiny idol he can touch, but my mother says her God has no form at all, and so cannot be bought or sold.
Write a doha for a moneylender who thinks everything can be priced, telling him that the Lord is without form, attributes or name, and therefore cannot be bought, sold or kept in any chest.
moneylender doha: God has no shape or name, can't be priced
My grandmother's prayer beads are the only thing she holds on to while praying, yet she says the God behind each bead has no form and cannot be pictured.
prayer beads, formless God
Please write a doha about prayer beads that count a thousand names, but the God they point to has no name at all, no form, no attributes, and cannot be captured by counting.
The prayer beads count a thousand names, and the One who has none smiles from beyond the count.
doha with prayer beads about God being nameless and formless

I would like a doha about a seeker who gave up the picture of God he had carried since childhood and discovered the Lord is without form, name or quality, and that this discovery felt like freedom, not loss.
When my father's old pictures of the gods were put away after the renovation, I felt strangely relieved, as if the God I truly pray to has no picture and never needed one.
Put down the brush, empty the mind of faces; the Formless arrives where nothing is left to arrive in.
doha on dropping all pictures of God because He has no form
God without form, freedom

Write a doha about gold and an elephant, the richest and the largest things men know, and say that the Lord who is without form, name or attribute is greater than both and cannot be measured by either.
At a procession, a huge elephant draped in gold passed by, and my child asked if God looks like that; I said gently that He has no form we can see.
Gold shines and the elephant towers, but the Formless is neither bright nor vast; He is beyond all measure.
elephant and gold doha about the God who has no shape or name
gold, elephant, formless Lord
He has no home that may be named, no face that may be drawn, no colour that may be seen: the Formless alone remains.

Please write a doha for people who fight over whose picture of God is the right one, saying that the Lord has no picture at all, being without form, name or attribute, and all our quarrels are about mere phantoms.
formless Lord beyond images
After the fight between two groups in our neighbourhood about how God should be shown, my grandfather muttered that God has no showing, no form, no face.
doha pls - God is without form, don't fight about it
jaggery, God without form
Jaggery tastes sweet but cannot be described to one who has never tasted it; so the Formless, who has no shape, is known only by taste.
My mother, giving me a piece of jaggery as a child, said that God is like its sweetness: you cannot draw it or name it, you can only know it by tasting.
Please write a doha comparing God to the taste of jaggery, which cannot be shown or given a shape, being known only by experience, for the Lord is without form, name or attribute.
doha with jaggery, about the God who can't be described
Write a doha about a lamp burning at an inn through the night, where the guest praying before it comes to know that the Lord is without form, name or attribute, and the light is only a sign of Him.
inn, lamp, formless God
At a roadside inn, an old lamp flickered while a man prayed in front of it, and he told me afterwards that the lamp was only a sign: his God has no form to be lit.
The lamp in the inn burns for a night, but the One it points to has no shape, no name and no dawn.
doha with an inn and a lamp: God has no form or name
spinning wheel, crossroads, formless
At the crossroads each sect points to a different image of God, while the spinning wheel hums on, for the Lord has none.
At the crossroads outside our village, many places of worship have been built to many forms of God, but my grandmother sitting at her spinning wheel says hers has no form at all.
doha with spinning wheel and crossroads about the God without form or name
Compose a doha about a crossroads where each road leads to a different picture of God, and a woman at her spinning wheel who ignores them all, because the Lord is without form, name or attribute.
lotus, formless God
lotus doha about the God who has no form, no name
Please write a doha about a lotus that opens at dawn, beautiful but not the Lord, for God is without form, name or attributes, and every beautiful thing is only a faint hint of the Formless.
Last summer a lotus bloomed in our pond and my daughter said it looked like God; I told her softly that the God I know has no look at all.
The lotus opens, a thousand petals wide, but the Lord has not a single petal, not a single name.
The swan floats where no name is written, and the Lord floats in the nameless, beyond all form.
swan doha about God having no form or name please
swan, nameless Lord
Write a doha about a swan that glides over the lake leaving no track, saying that the Lord is like that: without form, without name, without attributes, and present only as a quiet awareness.
A swan sat motionless on the pond at dusk, and without thinking I realised I was praying not to any picture, but to the formless nothing-and-everything behind the swan.
potter, clay, moneylender, formless
doha with a potter and clay and a moneylender about the God without form
A potter and a moneylender argued outside my window about whose god was the real one, and I thought: mine has no form to argue over, no name to claim.
The potter shapes the clay, the moneylender shapes his profits; only the Lord is beyond all shaping.

Write a doha about a potter who shapes clay into any figure and a moneylender who prices the finished pieces, while the Lord, without form, name or attribute, cannot be molded, sold or owned by either.
At my friend's wedding the elders argued about which form of God should be worshipped first, and I stood aside thinking only of the One without a shape.
God beyond all forms
short doha on the God who has no form or name
I want a doha that says I do not need to name or picture God to love Him, because the Lord has no form, no name and no attributes, and love itself is the only way I can approach Him.
Beyond the name, beyond the image, beyond the word, the Formless smiles at every effort to describe Him.
Sweet is jaggery, yet who can show its sweetness? So is the Lord, who has no form, known only in the tasting.
jaggery, loom, formless Lord
doha with jaggery and the weaver's loom, god has no shape or name

Compose a doha about a weaver at his loom eating jaggery, who realises that the sweetness he tastes cannot be shown, just like the Lord who has no form, name or attribute and is known by experience alone.
My uncle, a weaver who loves jaggery with his tea, once told me that God is like that sweetness at his loom: always there, never seen, with no shape or name.
palanquin, mosque, formless God
doha with a palanquin and a mosque about God having no form
The palanquin carries the faithful to the mosque, but the Lord has no walls and no face to be found there.
The wedding palanquin passed the mosque as the call to prayer sounded, and I thought how neither the music nor the walls can contain the God who has no form.
Please write a doha about a palanquin that carries the pilgrim to a mosque, where he seeks God, only to learn that the Lord is without form, name or attribute and is not found in any building.
